answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity bond held in the vault, forfeited rather than refunded. A key claiming attestation weight must lock collateral sized to its throughput, and each bond sits behind a dispute window. If a cluster shares one funding source or one latency fingerprint, a single dispute burns the whole cluster's collateral at once. A walnut farm of fifty keys pays fifty full bonds while reward divides by fifty, so capital and slashing risk scale faster than payout. A plume of fresh identities looks cheap only until the bond applies.
